text: Demand-side analyses that assume a proximate-consumption structure lose descriptive accuracy where the computative primitive holds, because most transactions occur among agents; welfare analysis in those domains must therefore be conducted at the terminal rather than the proximate level.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458

isBasedOn.name: Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance

abstract: The analytical consequence is that demand-side analyses that assume proximate-consumption structure lose descriptive accuracy in domains where the computative primitive holds. Welfare analysis in such domains must work at the terminal rather than proximate level.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: applies in domains where the computative primitive holds
